To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a model of renewable resource growth with a utility function that depends on both the level of the resource and consumption, the optimal consumption policy is monotonic and the optimal stock level is a nondecreasing, convex, and concave function of the resource.

(i) the optimal consumption, output, and investment processes are monotone, (ii) the optimal investment policy is proportional to the stock, (iii) the stock process is a diffusion process, (iv) the optimal consumption policy is proportional to a function of the stock, and (v) the limiting optimal consumption and output policies are linear in the stock.
in a stochastic aggregate growth model with stock-dependent utility, optimal policies are monotone and the limiting behavior of optimal policies is characterized by the deterministic model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of optimal consumption, investment and output policies in aggregate stochastic dynamic models with stock dependent utility and stock dependent production functions.
stochastic growth models with stock-dependent utility.
the study of stochastic growth models with stock-dependent utility functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the optimal consumption, output, and investment policies are monotonic, the optimal output process is asymptotically stationary, and the optimal investment process is asymptotical stationary or converges to a deterministic function.

the optimal consumption and investment strategies are monotone, and the optimal output process converges in distribution to a stationary Markov process with the long-run distribution being the unique stationary distribution of the stock process.
the optimal consumption, stock, and output processes are all monotonic, and that they converge to the steady-state solution as time tends to infinity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of stock-dependent utility, the optimal policy is a monotonic function of the state and, as a consequence of this fact, the optimal consumption and investment processes converge to the optimal consumption and capital processes in the case of constant relative risk aversion utility.
the optimal policies are monotone, and in the long run they converge to a steady state.
we have developed the stochastic dynamic programming theory of the aggregate growth model with stock-dependent utility.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stock-dependent utility models have a richer structure than models with utility only depending on consumption, and the stock variable can be an important state variable in the limiting behavior of the processes.

, when the stock-dependent component of utility is sufficiently small, then the optimal consumption and investment processes behave like the optimal policies in the standard growth model with no stock-dependent component of the utility function.
the presence of stock-dependent utility leads to a rich set of possible behaviors, including monotone and nonmonotone policies.
